source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Judges 13–21 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 243 original source records are bound exactly once.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated evaluation, divine handover and exact period.
verses.before: The children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
verses.after: Again the Israelites did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, and he gave them into the Philistines’ hand for forty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.

verses.rationale: Separate introduction from the repeated description of childlessness.
verses.before: There was a certain man from Zorah, from the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. His wife was barren and had not given birth.
verses.after: There was a man from Zorah, of the clan of Dan, named Manoah. His wife was barren and had borne no children.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a certain man from Zorah, from the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. His wife was barren and had not given birth.

verses.rationale: Retain the address to the woman and the contrast with her condition.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, “Look, you are barren and have not given birth, but you will conceive and give birth to a son.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said, “You are barren and have borne no children, but you will conceive and bear a son.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, “Look, you are barren and have not given birth, but you shall conceive and give birth to a son.

verses.rationale: Keep the dietary instructions directed to her, not silently transferred to the son.
verses.before: So now please be careful: do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.
verses.after: Now be careful: drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: So now please be careful: do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.

verses.rationale: Retain womb consecration and begin rather than a claim of complete liberation.
verses.before: For look, you will conceive and give birth to a son. No razor will come upon his head, for the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb. He will begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines.”
verses.after: You will conceive and bear a son. No razor is to touch his head, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb. He will begin to rescue Israel from the Philistines’ hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, you shall conceive and give birth to a son. No razor shall come upon his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb. He shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Keep her description distinct from the narrator’s identification.
verses.before: The woman came and told her husband, saying, “A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the messenger of God, very awe-inspiring. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.
verses.after: The woman went and told her husband, “A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God, very awe-inspiring. I did not ask where he came from, and he did not tell me his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman came and told her husband, saying, “A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the messenger of God, very awe-inspiring. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

verses.rationale: Preserve her retelling’s added lifelong duration rather than harmonizing the speeches.
verses.before: But he said to me, ‘Look, you will conceive and give birth to a son. So now do not drink wine or strong drink and do not eat anything unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.’”
verses.after: He told me, ‘You will conceive and bear a son. Drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day he dies.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said to me, ‘Look, you shall conceive and give birth to a son. So now do not drink wine or strong drink and do not eat anything unclean, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.’”

verses.rationale: Make the requested instruction audible without changing the prayer’s object.
verses.before: Then Manoah prayed to the LORD and said, “Please, Lord, let the man of God whom you sent come again to us and teach us what we should do for the boy who will be born.”
verses.after: Manoah pleaded with the LORD: “Please, Lord, let the man of God you sent come to us again and teach us what to do for the boy who will be born.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Manoah prayed to the LORD and said, “Please, Lord, let the man of God whom you sent come again to us and teach us what we should do for the boy who will be born.”

verses.rationale: Retain the second encounter with her despite the husband’s prayer.
verses.before: God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the messenger of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field. Manoah her husband was not with her.
verses.after: God listened to Manoah. The angel of God came to the woman again while she was sitting in the field; her husband Manoah was not with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the messenger of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field. Manoah her husband was not with her.

verses.rationale: Keep haste and her recognition of the previous visitor.
verses.before: The woman hurried and ran and told her husband, saying to him, “Look, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me.”
verses.after: She hurried and ran to tell her husband, “The man who came to me the other day has appeared to me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman hurried and ran and told her husband, saying to him, “Look, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me.”

verses.rationale: Keep the wife leading him and the direct identification.
verses.before: Manoah rose and followed his wife. He came to the man and said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to this woman?” He said, “I am.”
verses.after: Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he reached the man, he asked, “Are you the man who spoke to this woman?” “I am,” he answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Manoah rose and followed his wife. He came to the man and said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to this woman?” He said, “I am.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the two compressed questions about rule and work with alternatives noted.
verses.before: Manoah said, “Now when your words come to pass, what will be the rule for the boy and his work?”
verses.after: Manoah said, “When your words come true, how should the boy live, and what is he to do?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Manoah said, “Now when your words come to pass, what shall be the rule for the boy and his work?”

verses.rationale: Keep the response focused on her obligations rather than inventing instructions for the boy.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD said to Manoah, “The woman must be careful concerning everything I said to her.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD answered Manoah, “The woman must be careful about everything I told her.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD said to Manoah, “The woman must be careful concerning everything I said to her.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three restrictions and the repeated command to observe them.
verses.before: She will not eat anything that comes from the vine, nor drink wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean. Everything I commanded her, she will keep.”
verses.after: She must eat nothing that comes from the grapevine, drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean. She must observe everything I commanded her.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She shall not eat anything that comes from the vine, nor drink wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean. Everything I commanded her, she shall keep.”

verses.rationale: Render the invitation naturally while retaining the specific food.
verses.before: Manoah said to the messenger of the LORD, “Please let us detain you, and we will prepare a young goat for you.”
verses.after: Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “Please stay while we prepare a young goat for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Manoah said to the messenger of the LORD, “Please let us detain you, and we will prepare a young goat for you.”

verses.rationale: Distinguish hospitality from sacrifice and preserve the narrator’s explanation.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD said to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” For Manoah did not know that he was the messenger of the LORD.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD replied, “Even if you keep me here, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD said to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” For Manoah did not know that he was the messenger of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follow the read tradition’s singular word and the purpose of asking.
verses.before: Manoah said to the messenger of the LORD, “What is your name, so that when your words come to pass we may honor you?”
verses.after: Manoah asked the angel of the LORD, “What is your name? When your word comes true, we want to honor you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Manoah said to the messenger of the LORD, “What is your name, so that when your words come to pass we may honor you?”

verses.rationale: Render the extraordinary-name expression without turning it into a fixed proper name.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD said to him, “Why do you ask my name, seeing that it is wonderful?”
verses.after: The angel of the LORD answered, “Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD said to him, “Why do you ask my name, seeing that it is wonderful?”

verses.rationale: Preserve the compressed divine action and its link to the wonderful-name wording.
verses.before: So Manoah took the young goat with the grain offering and offered it upon the rock to the LORD, to the one who works wonders. Manoah and his wife were watching.
verses.after: Manoah took the young goat and the grain offering and offered them on the rock to the LORD. The LORD did something wondrous while Manoah and his wife watched.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Manoah took the young goat with the grain offering and offered it upon the rock to the LORD, to the one who works wonders. Manoah and his wife were watching.

verses.rationale: Keep the movement in the flame and both witnesses’ response.
verses.before: When the flame went up toward heaven from the altar, the messenger of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife were watching, and they fell on their faces to the ground.
verses.after: As the flame rose from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the LORD went up in the altar’s flame. Manoah and his wife saw it and fell facedown to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the flame went up toward heaven from the altar, the messenger of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife were watching, and they fell on their faces to the ground.

verses.rationale: Retain the delayed recognition rather than announcing it earlier for him.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD appeared no more to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the messenger of the LORD.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD did not appear to Manoah and his wife again. Then Manoah knew that he was the angel of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD appeared no more to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the messenger of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the inference as Manoah’s speech.
verses.before: Manoah said to his wife, “We will surely die, for we have seen God.”
verses.after: “We will surely die,” Manoah told his wife, “because we have seen God!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Manoah said to his wife, “We shall surely die, for we have seen God.”

verses.rationale: Let her three-part reasoning answer his fear without added commentary.
verses.before: But his wife said to him, “If the LORD had desired to put us to death, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hand, or shown us all these things, or now announced such things to us.”
verses.after: But his wife answered, “If the LORD wanted to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hands, shown us all this, or told us these things now.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But his wife said to him, “If the LORD had desired to put us to death, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hand, or shown us all these things, or now announced such things to us.”

verses.rationale: Retain her agency in naming and the growth/blessing sequence.
verses.before: The woman gave birth to a son and called his name Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.
verses.after: The woman bore a son and named him Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman gave birth to a son and called his name Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.

verses.rationale: Keep began, the Spirit and both geographic endpoints.
verses.before: And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh-Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.after: The Spirit of the LORD began to stir him at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh-Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

verses.rationale: Retain seeing and the woman’s people as the story’s opening emphasis.
verses.before: Samson went down to Timnah, and at Timnah he saw a woman from the daughters of the Philistines.
verses.after: Samson went down to Timnah and saw a woman there, one of the daughters of the Philistines.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samson went down to Timnah, and at Timnah he saw a woman from the daughters of the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Keep both parents addressed and Samson’s imperative.
verses.before: He went up and told his father and mother, saying, “I have seen a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines. Now therefore get her for me as wife.”
verses.after: He went up and told his father and mother, “I saw a woman in Timnah, one of the Philistine women. Now get her for me as my wife.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He went up and told his father and mother, saying, “I have seen a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines. Now therefore get her for me as wife.”

verses.rationale: Preserve uncircumcised and right-in-eyes language linking personal desire with the book’s refrain.
verses.before: His father and mother said to him, “Is there no woman among the daughters of your relatives or among all my people, that you must go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” Samson said to his father, “Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes.”
verses.after: His father and mother asked, “Is there no woman among your relatives or all my people, that you must go and take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” Samson told his father, “Get her for me. She is right in my eyes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His father and mother said to him, “Is there no woman among the daughters of your relatives or among all my people, that you must go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” Samson said to his father, “Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes.”

verses.rationale: Choose the LORD as the seeking subject while noting the pronoun’s possible reference to Samson.
verses.before: His father and mother did not know that this was from the LORD, for he was seeking an occasion against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
verses.after: His father and mother did not know that this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: His father and mother did not know that this was from the LORD, for he was seeking an occasion against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the companions and the sudden singular encounter without inventing a separation.
verses.before: Then Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnah. When they came to the vineyards of Timnah, look, a young lion came roaring toward him.
verses.after: Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. As they reached Timnah’s vineyards, a young lion came roaring toward him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnah. When they came to the vineyards of Timnah, look, a young lion came roaring toward him.

verses.rationale: Retain the violent simile, empty hand and concealed action.
verses.before: The Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he tore the lion apart as one tears apart a young goat, though he had nothing in his hand. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
verses.after: The Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he tore the lion apart as one tears a young goat. He had nothing in his hand. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he tore the lion apart as one tears apart a young goat, though he had nothing in his hand. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.

verses.rationale: Repeat the eyes formula rather than replacing it with an unrelated emotion.
verses.before: He went down and spoke with the woman, and she was right in Samson’s eyes.
verses.after: He went down and spoke with the woman, and she was right in Samson’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went down and spoke with the woman, and she was right in Samson’s eyes.

verses.rationale: Keep the return and surprising contents without explaining their natural history.
verses.before: After some days he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion. Look, there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.
verses.after: Some time later he returned to marry her. He turned aside to look at the lion’s remains, and there was a swarm of bees in its carcass, with honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: After some days he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion. Look, there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.

verses.rationale: Preserve the concealed origin and parental participation without inserting an accusation.
verses.before: He scraped some into his hands and went on, eating as he went. He came to his father and mother and gave some to them, and they ate. But he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey from the body of the lion.
verses.after: He scooped the honey into his hands and ate as he walked. When he reached his father and mother, he gave them some, and they ate. He did not tell them he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass.
verses.tsw_comparator: He scraped some into his hands and went on, eating as he went. He came to his father and mother and gave some to them, and they ate. But he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey from the body of the lion.

verses.rationale: Keep the father as the first subject and Samson as host.
verses.before: His father went down to the woman, and Samson held a feast there, for so the young men used to do.
verses.after: His father went down to the woman, and Samson held a feast there, as young men customarily did.
verses.tsw_comparator: His father went down to the woman, and Samson held a feast there, for so the young men used to do.

verses.rationale: Supply only the local people for the unspecified plural, retaining the source’s saw.
verses.before: When they saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.
verses.after: When the people there saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.

verses.rationale: Keep the conditions, deadline and two distinct clothing categories.
verses.before: Samson said to them, “Let me tell you a riddle. If you can surely explain it to me within the seven days of the feast and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.
verses.after: Samson told them, “Let me give you a riddle. If you solve it and tell me the answer within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samson said to them, “Let me tell you a riddle. If you can surely explain it to me within the seven days of the feast and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.

verses.rationale: Repeat the full wager and make the response’s speaker clear.
verses.before: But if you cannot explain it to me, then you will give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.” They said to him, “Tell your riddle, and let us hear it.”
verses.after: But if you cannot tell me the answer, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.” They said, “Tell us your riddle. Let us hear it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you cannot explain it to me, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.” They said to him, “Tell your riddle, and let us hear it.”

verses.rationale: Preserve parallel riddle lines and the three-day impasse within the verse paragraph.
verses.before: He said to them: “Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.” For three days they could not explain the riddle.
verses.after: He said, “Out of the eater came food; out of the strong came sweetness.” For three days they could not solve the riddle.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them: “Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.” For three days they could not explain the riddle.

verses.rationale: Keep the pinned seventh day with the fourth-day variant noted and the lethal threat explicit.
verses.before: On the seventh day they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband to explain the riddle to us, lest we burn you and your father’s house with fire. Have you invited us here to impoverish us?”
verses.after: On the seventh day they told Samson’s wife, “Persuade your husband to tell us the answer, or we will burn you and your father’s household. Did you invite us here to make us poor?”
verses.tsw_comparator: On the seventh day they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband to explain the riddle to us, lest we burn you and your father’s house with fire. Have you invited us here to impoverish us?”

verses.rationale: Preserve her appeal and his comparison with his parents.
verses.before: Samson’s wife wept before him and said, “You only hate me; you do not love me. You have told a riddle to the children of my people but have not explained it to me.” He said to her, “Look, I have not explained it to my father or mother; should I explain it to you?”
verses.after: Samson’s wife wept before him. “You only hate me; you do not love me,” she said. “You gave my people a riddle, but you have not told me the answer.” He replied, “I have not even told my father or mother. Should I tell you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samson’s wife wept before him and said, “You only hate me; you do not love me. You have told a riddle to the children of my people but have not explained it to me.” He said to her, “Look, I have not explained it to my father or mother; should I explain it to you?”

verses.rationale: Retain all seven days without repairing the earlier timeline; keep pressure distinct from its motive.
verses.before: She wept before him the seven days while their feast lasted. On the seventh day he explained it to her because she pressed him hard. Then she explained the riddle to the children of her people.
verses.after: She wept before him throughout the seven days of their feast. On the seventh day he told her because she pressed him so hard, and she told her people the answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: She wept before him the seven days while their feast lasted. On the seventh day he explained it to her because she pressed him hard. Then she explained the riddle to the children of her people.

verses.rationale: Keep both poetic replies and the demeaning heifer image in Samson’s voice.
verses.before: The men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down: “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” He said to them: “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle.”
verses.after: Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the town said to him, “What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?” He answered, “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down: “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” He said to them: “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle.”

verses.rationale: Keep Spirit, killing and payment together without turning the violence into moral endorsement.
verses.before: Then the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck thirty men of the city, took their plunder, and gave the changes of clothing to people who had explained the riddle. His anger burned, and he went up to his father’s house.
verses.after: The Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him. He went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty men there, stripped them, and gave their clothes to those who had solved the riddle. Burning with anger, he went up to his father’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck thirty men of the city, took their plunder, and gave the changes of clothing to those who had explained the riddle. His anger burned, and he went up to his father’s house.

verses.rationale: Retain the transfer and companion relationship without imposing the modern title best man.
verses.before: Samson’s wife was given to his companion, who had been his best man.
verses.after: Samson’s wife was given to the companion who had attended him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Samson’s wife was given to his companion, who had been his best man.

verses.rationale: Preserve the harvest setting, gift and blocked marital visit.
verses.before: After some days, during the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat. He said, “I will go in to my wife in the chamber.” But her father would not allow him to go in.
verses.after: Some time later, during the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat. “I will go in to my wife in her room,” he said. But her father would not let him enter.
verses.tsw_comparator: After some days, during the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat. He said, “I will go in to my wife in the chamber.” But her father would not allow him to go in.

verses.rationale: Retain the father’s assumption and offer of another daughter as his actions.
verses.before: Her father said, “I truly thought that you utterly hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.”
verses.after: Her father said, “I was sure you hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister more attractive than she is? Please take her instead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Her father said, “I truly thought that you utterly hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.”

verses.rationale: Keep the claim to innocence in Samson’s mouth rather than the narrator’s judgment.
verses.before: Samson said to them, “This time I will be innocent regarding the Philistines when I do harm to them.”
verses.after: Samson told them, “This time I will be blameless when I harm the Philistines.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samson said to them, “This time I shall be innocent regarding the Philistines when I do harm to them.”

verses.rationale: Retain number and method; note foxes or jackals without inventing capture details.
verses.before: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, took torches, turned tail to tail, and put a torch between each pair of tails.
verses.after: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes. He took torches, turned the animals tail to tail, and placed a torch between each pair of tails.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, took torches, turned tail to tail, and put a torch between each pair of tails.

verses.rationale: Preserve each crop category and the spread of fire.
verses.before: When he had set the torches on fire, he released them into the standing grain of the Philistines and burned up both the stacked grain and standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.
verses.after: He lit the torches and released the animals into the Philistines’ standing grain. He burned the stacked grain, the standing crops, and the olive orchards.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he had set the torches on fire, he released them into the standing grain of the Philistines and burned up both the stacked grain and standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.

verses.rationale: Make kinship clear and retain the killing of the threatened woman and father.

verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin on the third day and arranged themselves against Gibeah as at other times.

verses.rationale: Preserve both named routes, open-country setting and approximate casualties; note uncertain geography.
verses.before: The children of Benjamin went out against the people and were drawn away from the city. They began to strike and kill some of the people as at other times, on the highways, one of which goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, and in the field, about thirty men of Israel.
verses.after: The Benjaminites came out to meet the army and were drawn away from the town. As before, they began killing Israelites along the roads—one leading to Bethel, the other toward Gibeah—and in the open country. About thirty Israelites fell.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Benjamin went out against the people and were drawn away from the city. They began to strike and kill some of the people as at other times, on the highways, one of which goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, and in the field, about thirty men of Israel.

verses.rationale: Contrast mistaken interpretation with the stated plan.
verses.before: The children of Benjamin said, “They are being defeated before us as at first.” But the children of Israel said, “Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways.”
verses.after: The Benjaminites said, “They are being defeated before us as before.” But the Israelites had said, “Let us retreat and draw them away from the town onto the roads.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Benjamin said, “They are being defeated before us as at first.” But the children of Israel said, “Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways.”

verses.rationale: Keep the two forces and difficult terrain phrase with alternatives noted.
verses.before: Then all the men of Israel rose from their place and arranged themselves at Baal-Tamar, while the ambush of Israel burst out from its place at Maareh-Geba.
verses.after: All Israel’s men rose from their positions and formed their line at Baal-tamar. Meanwhile, Israel’s ambush force burst from its position in the open ground near Geba.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the men of Israel rose from their place and arranged themselves at Baal-Tamar, while the ambush of Israel burst out from its place at Maareh-Geba.

verses.rationale: Preserve exact contingent, intensity and lack of knowledge.
verses.before: Ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came against Gibeah, and the battle was fierce. But the Benjaminites did not know that disaster was about to touch them.
verses.after: Ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came against Gibeah. The battle was fierce, and the Benjaminites did not know disaster was closing in on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came against Gibeah, and the battle was fierce. But the Benjaminites did not know that disaster was about to touch them.

verses.rationale: Keep divine agency and summary total distinct from the later twenty-five thousand.
verses.before: The LORD struck Benjamin before Israel, and the children of Israel destroyed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin that day, everyone who drew the sword.
verses.after: The LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel. That day the Israelites struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all swordsmen.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD struck Benjamin before Israel, and the children of Israel destroyed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin that day, all who drew the sword.

verses.rationale: Mark the retrospective explanation naturally without deleting the repeated account.
verses.before: So the children of Benjamin saw that they were defeated. The men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin because they trusted in the ambush they had set against Gibeah.
verses.after: The Benjaminites saw that they were defeated. Israel’s men had given ground to Benjamin because they trusted the ambush they had placed against Gibeah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the children of Benjamin saw that they were defeated. The men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin because they trusted in the ambush they had set against Gibeah.

verses.rationale: Retain the compressed second movement and total scope of attack.
verses.before: The men in ambush hurried and rushed upon Gibeah. The ambush advanced and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.
verses.after: The ambush force rushed into Gibeah, spread through it, and struck the whole town with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men in ambush hurried and rushed upon Gibeah. The ambush advanced and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.

verses.rationale: Keep the specific coordinated signal.
verses.before: Now the appointed signal between the men of Israel and the ambush was that they would make a great cloud of smoke rise from the city.
verses.after: The agreed signal between Israel’s men and the ambush force was to send up a great cloud of smoke from the town.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the appointed signal between the men of Israel and the ambush was that they would make a great cloud of smoke rise from the city.

verses.rationale: Read turned as the feigned retreat here, with the other turn in 41, and retain the repeated thirty.
verses.before: Then the men of Israel turned in the battle. Benjamin began to strike and kill about thirty men of Israel, for they said, “Surely they are being defeated before us as in the first battle.”
verses.after: Israel’s men had turned back in the battle, and Benjamin had begun to kill about thirty of them. “They are certainly being defeated before us, just as in the first battle,” Benjamin said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the men of Israel turned in the battle. Benjamin began to strike and kill about thirty men of Israel, for they said, “Surely they are being defeated before us as in the first battle.”

verses.rationale: Retain rising smoke and the whole-town image without introducing a new battle.
verses.before: But when the cloud began to rise from the city, a pillar of smoke, the Benjaminites looked behind them, and look, the whole city was going up in smoke toward heaven.
verses.after: Then the cloud began rising from the town, a pillar of smoke. Benjamin looked back: the whole town was going up toward heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the cloud began to rise from the city, a pillar of smoke, the Benjaminites looked behind them, and look, the whole city was going up in smoke toward heaven.

verses.rationale: Keep the decisive reversal and recognition.
verses.before: Then the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that disaster had touched them.
verses.after: Israel’s men turned around, and the Benjaminites were terrified. They saw that disaster had reached them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that disaster had touched them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the difficult plural towns and unspecified attackers, with alternatives noted.
verses.before: So they turned before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them. People who came out of the cities destroyed them in their midst.
verses.after: They turned away from Israel’s men toward the wilderness, but the battle overtook them. Those coming from the towns struck them down in their midst.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they turned before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them. Those who came out of the cities destroyed them in their midst.

verses.rationale: Retain the uncertain rest expression and eastward endpoint without forcing a place name.
verses.before: They surrounded Benjamin, pursued him, and trampled him down from Nohah as far as opposite Gibeah toward the sunrise.
verses.after: They surrounded Benjamin, pursued him, and trampled him at his resting place, as far as the area east of Gibeah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They surrounded Benjamin, pursued him, and trampled him down from Nohah as far as opposite Gibeah toward the sunrise.

verses.rationale: Keep this stage’s number and description.
verses.before: Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all of them men of valor.
verses.after: Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all capable warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all of them men of valor.

verses.rationale: Retain the gleaning metaphor, both loss figures and named destinations.
verses.before: They turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and Israel gleaned five thousand men from them on the highways. They pursued closely after them as far as Gidom and struck two thousand men from them.
verses.after: The survivors turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. Israel gleaned five thousand men along the roads, then pursued them as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand more.
verses.tsw_comparator: They turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and Israel gleaned five thousand men from them on the highways. They pursued closely after them as far as Gidom and struck two thousand men from them.

verses.rationale: Keep this summary figure without silently harmonizing verse 35.
verses.before: So everyone who fell from Benjamin that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword, all of them men of valor.
verses.after: In all, twenty-five thousand swordsmen of Benjamin fell that day, all capable warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all who fell from Benjamin that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword, all of them men of valor.

verses.rationale: Preserve survivor count and duration.
verses.before: But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon and stayed at the rock of Rimmon four months.
verses.after: Six hundred men turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon. They stayed there four months.
verses.tsw_comparator: But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon and stayed at the rock of Rimmon four months.

verses.rationale: Preserve indiscriminate destruction beyond the army, with the difficult whole-town phrase noted.
verses.before: Then the men of Israel turned back against the children of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from the city to the animals and all that was found. They also set on fire every city they came to.
verses.after: Israel’s men turned back against the Benjaminites and struck them with the sword—whole towns, livestock, everything they found. They also set fire to every town they came upon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the men of Israel turned back against the children of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from the city to the animals and all that was found. They also set on fire every city they came to.

verses.rationale: Introduce the prior oath and its specific prohibition on giving daughters.
verses.before: Now the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, “None of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as wife.”
verses.after: At Mizpah Israel’s men had sworn, “None of us will give his daughter to a Benjaminite as a wife.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, “None of us shall give his daughter to Benjamin as wife.”

verses.rationale: Keep place, duration and loud communal grief.
verses.before: The people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening. They lifted up their voices and wept greatly.
verses.after: The people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening. They raised their voices and wept bitterly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening. They lifted up their voices and wept greatly.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated Israel and their question without absolving their role.
verses.before: They said, “Why, O LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?”
verses.after: “LORD, God of Israel,” they said, “why has this happened in Israel, that one tribe should be missing from Israel today?”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “Why, O LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?”

verses.rationale: Keep timing and both offering types.
verses.before: The next day the people rose early and built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and offerings of well-being.
verses.after: Early the next morning the people built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and well-being offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: The next day the people rose early and built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and offerings of well-being.

verses.rationale: Keep the second oath as the assembly’s own and the lethal consequence.
verses.before: The children of Israel said, “Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come up in the assembly to the LORD?” For they had made a great oath concerning anyone who did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah, saying, “He will surely be put to death.”
verses.after: The Israelites asked, “Who from all Israel’s tribes failed to come up to the assembly before the LORD?” For they had sworn a solemn oath that anyone who failed to come before the LORD at Mizpah must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel said, “Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come up in the assembly to the LORD?” For they had made a great oath concerning anyone who did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah, saying, “He shall surely be put to death.”

verses.rationale: Retain brother language and cut-off image.
verses.before: The children of Israel had compassion on Benjamin their brother and said, “One tribe has been cut off from Israel today.
verses.after: The Israelites grieved for their brother Benjamin. “Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel,” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel had compassion on Benjamin their brother and said, “One tribe has been cut off from Israel today.

verses.rationale: Keep their problem defined by the oath rather than by a divine command.
verses.before: What will we do for wives for people who remain, since we have sworn by the LORD that we will not give them any of our daughters as wives?”
verses.after: “What can we do to provide wives for the survivors? We have sworn by the LORD not to give them our daughters as wives.”
verses.tsw_comparator: What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since we have sworn by the LORD that we will not give them any of our daughters as wives?”

verses.rationale: Make the inquiry and its finding distinct.
verses.before: They said, “What one from the tribes of Israel did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah?” And look, no one had come to the camp from Jabesh-Gilead to the assembly.
verses.after: They asked, “Which group from Israel’s tribes did not come before the LORD at Mizpah?” It turned out that no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp for the assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “What one from the tribes of Israel did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah?” And look, no one had come to the camp from Jabesh-Gilead to the assembly.

verses.rationale: Preserve verification of absence despite repetition.
verses.before: For when the people were counted, look, none of the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead was there.
verses.after: When the people were counted, no one from Jabesh-gilead was there.
verses.tsw_comparator: For when the people were counted, look, none of the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead was there.

verses.rationale: Keep the assembly as commander, exact force and named noncombatants.
verses.before: So the congregation sent twelve thousand of the men of valor there and commanded them, saying, “Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead with the edge of the sword, including the women and little children.
verses.after: The congregation sent twelve thousand warriors there and commanded them, “Go and strike the people of Jabesh-gilead with the sword, including the women and children.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the congregation sent twelve thousand of the men of valor there and commanded them, saying, “Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead with the edge of the sword, including the women and little children.

verses.rationale: Retain the ban language and sex-based distinction with its lethal meaning explicit.
verses.before: This is the thing you will do: devote to destruction every male and every woman who has known the lying of a male.”
verses.after: This is what you must do: devote to destruction every male and every woman who has slept with a man.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the thing you shall do: devote to destruction every male and every woman who has known the lying of a male.”

verses.rationale: Keep number, sexual criterion and forced movement without calling it rescue.
verses.before: They found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead four hundred young virgins who had not known a man by lying with a male, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
verses.after: Among the people of Jabesh-gilead they found four hundred young virgins who had not slept with a man. They brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: They found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead four hundred young virgins who had not known a man by lying with a male, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Preserve collective peace offer and location.
verses.before: Then the whole congregation sent and spoke to the children of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.
verses.after: The whole congregation sent word to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the whole congregation sent and spoke to the children of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.

verses.rationale: Keep transfer of captive women and the shortage without adding a count here.
verses.before: Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive from the women of Jabesh-Gilead. But there were not enough for them.
verses.after: Benjamin returned at that time, and the Israelites gave them the women they had kept alive from Jabesh-gilead. But there were not enough for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive from the women of Jabesh-Gilead. But there were not enough for them.

verses.rationale: Retain the narrator’s attribution and breach image without omitting human actions around it.
verses.before: The people had compassion on Benjamin because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
verses.after: The people grieved for Benjamin because the LORD had made a breach in Israel’s tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people had compassion on Benjamin because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the women’s destruction and clarify which survivors remain without wives.
verses.before: Then the elders of the congregation said, “What will we do for wives for people who remain, since the women have been destroyed from Benjamin?”
verses.after: The elders of the congregation said, “What can we do to provide wives for the men still without them? The women of Benjamin have been destroyed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the elders of the congregation said, “What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since the women have been destroyed from Benjamin?”

verses.rationale: Retain the compressed inheritance claim with a minimal supplied predicate.
verses.before: They said, “There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe may not be blotted out from Israel.
verses.after: They said, “There must be an inheritance for Benjamin’s survivors, so that a tribe is not wiped out of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe may not be blotted out from Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve the speakers’ constraint and explanatory curse.
verses.before: Yet we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for the children of Israel had sworn, saying, ‘Cursed is the one who gives a wife to Benjamin.’”
verses.after: But we cannot give them wives from our daughters.” For the Israelites had sworn, “Cursed is anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for the children of Israel had sworn, saying, ‘Cursed is the one who gives a wife to Benjamin.’”

verses.rationale: Keep all three geographic bearings and the unspecified festival.
verses.before: So they said, “Look, there is the yearly festival of the LORD at Shiloh, which is north of Bethel, east of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”
verses.after: Then they said, “There is a yearly festival of the LORD at Shiloh, north of Bethel, east of the road from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So they said, “Look, there is the yearly festival of the LORD at Shiloh, which is north of Bethel, east of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”

verses.rationale: Follow the plural read tradition and keep elders as instructors, not God.
verses.before: They commanded the children of Benjamin, saying, “Go and lie in wait in the vineyards.
verses.after: They instructed the Benjaminites, “Go and hide in the vineyards.
verses.tsw_comparator: They commanded the children of Benjamin, saying, “Go and lie in wait in the vineyards.

verses.rationale: Preserve the planned abduction and the women’s activity without recasting it as courtship.
verses.before: Watch, and look, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out from the vineyards, seize for yourselves each man his wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
verses.after: Watch for the daughters of Shiloh to come out dancing. Then come out of the vineyards, each of you seize a wife from Shiloh’s daughters, and go to the land of Benjamin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Watch, and look, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out from the vineyards, seize for yourselves each man his wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

verses.rationale: Choose a coherent reading of the compressed plea and oath loophole, marking its uncertainty in a note.
verses.before: When their fathers or brothers come to complain to us, we will say to them, ‘Show us favor concerning them, because we did not take a wife for each man in battle, and you did not give them to them, or you would now be guilty.’”
verses.after: If their fathers or brothers come to dispute with us, we will tell them, ‘Be gracious to us and let them keep the women. We did not take a wife for each man in the war. You did not give the women to them; otherwise you would now be guilty.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: When their fathers or brothers come to complain to us, we will say to them, ‘Show us favor concerning them, because we did not take a wife for each man in battle, and you did not give them to them, or you would now be guilty.’”

verses.rationale: Keep violent taking explicit and distinct from the subsequent settlement.
verses.before: The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number from the women who danced, whom they carried away. Then they went and returned to their inheritance, rebuilt the cities, and lived in them.
verses.after: The Benjaminites did this. They carried off enough of the dancing women to be their wives. Then they went back to their inheritance, rebuilt the towns, and settled in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number from the women who danced, whom they carried away. Then they went and returned to their inheritance, rebuilt the cities, and lived in them.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated distribution to tribe, clan and inheritance.
verses.before: The children of Israel departed from there at that time, each to his tribe and clan. They went out from there, each to his inheritance.
verses.after: At that time the Israelites left, each for his own tribe and clan. Each went from there to his own inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel departed from there at that time, each to his tribe and clan. They went out from there, each to his inheritance.

verses.rationale: Repeat the exact closing refrain and its eyes image.
verses.before: In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in their own eyes.
verses.after: In those days Israel had no king. Everyone did what was right in their own eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in their own eyes.
